title: Precision fleet supply blend optimizer
content:
Executive summary:
This worksheet explores an optimized fleet composition (the "blend") across precision tiers and batching strategies to meet Q1 2029 regional SLAs while minimizing $/generated-token and bounding observable quality regressions on our eval suites. The goal is a pragmatic mix of low-bit (4-bit/INT4), mid-bit (8-bit/INT8), and high-precision nodes to serve our typical production mix: 60% short-chat, 30% assistant-longform, 10% embedding/reprompt workloads.

Scope and objective:
- Time horizon: January–March 2029 capacity planning horizon (prep for sales commitments and Dedicated reservations).
- Regions: NA, EU, APAC (priority APAC capacity lift).
- Deliverable: suggested percent allocation per region to each precision tier + recommended batching target ranges and KV cache settings.

Key assumptions (baseline workload):
- 80M-1B token/month aggregate projected growth + seasonal peak at +28% in Feb.
- Request distribution by sequence length: p50=64 tokens, p90=320 tokens, p99=1,200 tokens.
- Latency SLO: 95% requests < 400ms for NA/EU, 500ms for APAC.
- KV cache hit rate (prefix reuse): baseline 18% global, with targeted improvements to 28% for assistant routes after cache warmups.
- Model variants: Open-family LMs with identical model architecture served in FP16 (high-quality), INT8 (good), and INT4/QLoRA* (low-bit) builds.
- Quality metric: delta on core assistant eval (answer_f1) relative to FP16 baseline. We consider a -2.0 pts drop acceptable; beyond -3.5 pts is high risk.

Throughput and quality characterization (empirical inputs):
- Per-GPU steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) estimates (measured on typical A100-like nodes, continuous batching):
  * FP16 (high-precision): p50 latency tight; tokens/sec = 1.0x baseline, cost multiplier = 1.00, quality delta = 0.0
  * INT8: tokens/sec = 1.9x, cost multiplier = 0.55, quality delta = -0.6 pts
  * INT4 (low-bit): tokens/sec = 3.6x, cost multiplier = 0.32, quality delta = -2.8 pts
- Batching sensitivity (sequence-length-weighted): throughput gains plateau beyond batch size 48 for short requests and beyond 12 for long-form (due to memory/KV constraints).
- Tail latency cost: pushing batching aggressively increases p95 latency by +40–120ms depending on sequence mix; risk threshold at +80ms.

Regional capacity constraints and supply plan:
- NA: existing reserved pool can scale +30% by rebalancing mid-bit nodes; procurement lead time 6–8 weeks.
- EU: limited procurement; recommend converting 12% of FP16 to burstable INT8 nodes for immediate uplift.
- APAC: constrained by both capacity and cost; target heavier low-bit adoption to increase throughput while routing higher-precision bursts from regional partner zones for critical routes.

Candidate fleet blends (per-region recommendations):
- Conservative (low risk, higher cost): FP16 50% | INT8 40% | INT4 10%
  * Expected fleet throughput multiplier vs current = 1.45x, estimated quality delta = -0.5 pts, cost reduction ~18%
- Balanced (recommended for NA/EU): FP16 30% | INT8 50% | INT4 20%
  * Throughput multiplier = 2.05x, quality delta = -1.2 pts, cost reduction ~38%
- Aggressive (APAC-focused, cost-prioritized): FP16 15% | INT8 35% | INT4 50%
  * Throughput multiplier = 2.86x, quality delta = -2.3 pts, cost reduction ~57%

Routing and runtime policies to mitigate quality regressions:
- SLO-aware routing: prefer FP16/INT8 for routes tagged high-quality (customer-premium, 5% traffic).
- Dynamic fallback: if INT4 p95 crosses +80ms over baseline, shift requests to INT8 in-region; if INT8 degraded, fall back to FP16 cross-region (with cost accounting).
- Canary windows: new low-bit nodes enter canary with 1% traffic and automated eval hooks against the assistant eval suite for the first 72 hours.

Sensitivity analysis (what breaks and mitigation):
- If assistant eval delta worsens > -3.5 pts on INT4: cap INT4 at <=30% fleet and require retraining/LoRA tuning before expansion.
- If KV cache hit drops by >8pp (e.g., from 28% to 20%): effective throughput falls ~9%; schedule targeted prefix cache optimization tickets.
- If APAC demand growth exceeds 40% peak: activate cross-region spillover and increase INT8 burst pool size by +25%.

Quick calculation examples (simplified):
- Baseline monthly tokens = 1.0B tokens. Target cost reduction = 40%.
  * Balanced blend throughput multiplier = 2.05x => required GPUs = baseline_gpus / 2.05. With cost multipliers this yields ~38% cost reduction vs pure FP16 after accounting for model pricing and utilization improvements. (See detailed workbook links below.)

Operational checklist and next actions:
- [ ] Spin dedicated canaries in APAC (3 INT4 nodes, 2 INT8 nodes) and run eval harness (owner: Liam). Target start: 2028-12-18.
- [ ] Add route-level "quality_priority" tag to top 30 customer routes for routing policy (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Create ticket INFRA-8429: KV cache telemetry dashboard for per-route hit rates and eviction behavior (owner: Jonas).
- [ ] Finance: run pricing sensitivity with 3rd party procurement quotes for A100-like vs newer low-power accelerators (owner: Ava).

Open questions / risks:
- Long-term: does INT4 quality gap decline after additional quant-aware fine-tuning? If yes, aggressive tilt becomes higher confidence.
- Legal/regulatory: cross-region fallback may require additional data processing agreements for some EU/enterprise customers.
- Observability: we need per-precision per-route quality tagging in the logs to correlate customer regressions to precision tier.

Attachments and references:
- Linked perf workbook: CONFLUENCE: /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=98765432 (contains per-GPU throughput sheets and cost assumptions).
- Empirical traces: GITHUB: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1643 (bench harness and scripts).
- JIRA baseline ticket: INFRA-8421 (fleet procurement plan).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working worksheet intended to spark tradeoff discussion with product and finance before we lock dedicated reservations. Values are intentionally round-tripped from measured runs but should be validated against the detailed benchmark workbook before executive sign-off.
